accounts.account: Israel states it has responded to Palestinian needs and increased water quantities provided beyond the Interim Agreement specifications; however, 60% of water provided is sold to Palestinians at inflated prices[citation:5]

Palestinian sources report discriminatory distribution: Israel uses 85% of water from West Bank aquifers, Palestinians receive 15%. Per capita use in Israel is 3.5 times higher than in the West Bank. Under international law, expropriating water from occupied territories for use by Israeli citizens is illegal.[citation:5]

Israel advances settlement construction for civilian and security purposes; the Civil Administration views Area C as serving Israeli needs including military training, economic interests, and settlement development[citation:1]

Israeli settlements in the West Bank are considered illegal under international law; settlement expansion undermines a future Palestinian state. As of 2025-2026, more than 700,000 settlers live in the West Bank including East Jerusalem. Israel advanced plans for 2,377 housing units between December 1, 2024 and January 2025 alone.[citation:1][citation:8][citation:9]

accounts.account: تدعي إسرائيل أنها استجابت لاحتياجات الفلسطينيين وزودتهم بكميات مياه تفوق ما هو منصوص عليه في الاتفاقية المرحلية، لكن 60% من المياه الموردة تبيعها بأسعار مرتفعة [citation:11].

وفقاً للمصادر الفلسطينية والدولية، تستخدم إسرائيل 85% من مياه الأحواض الجوفية في الضفة الغربية بينما يحصل الفلسطينيون على 15% فقط. استهلاك الفرد في إسرائيل أعلى بثلاثة أضعاف ونصف من الضفة الغربية. يمنع الفلسطينيون من حفر آبار جديدة دون تصاريح إسرائيلية شبه مستحيلة الحصول عليها. الهدم المتكرر للآبار والخزانات: منذ 2021، هدمت السلطات الإسرائيلية ما يقرب من 160 خزاناً وشبكة صرف صحي وبئراً في الضفة الغربية والقدس الشرقية بدعوى عدم الترخيص [citation:11][citation:15].

accounts.account: تقدم إسرائيل البناء الاستيطاني لأغراض مدنية وأمنية [citation:1].

المصادر الفلسطينية توثق أن الاستيطان الإسرائيلي في الضفة الغربية غير قانوني بموجب القانون الدولي. في 2024، تم إنشاء 60 بؤرة استيطانية عشوائية (ضعف عدد 2023). بين 1996 وأوائل 2023، كان المتوسط أقل من 7 بؤر سنوياً [citation:2]. في فبراير 2026، وافقت الحكومة الإسرائيلية على استئناف عملية تسجيل الأراضي في الضفة لأول مرة منذ 1967، وهو ما تصفه منظمات حقوقية إسرائيلية بأنه "إضفاء منهجية على تهجير الفلسطينيين" حيث أن 70% من أراضي الضفة غير مسجلة وغير مثبتة الملكية للفلسطينيين [citation:8].

legal.name: June 2004 Ruling on Separation Barrier Route (2004) — Israel Supreme Court (Bagatz)
legal.desc: Ruled that a portion of the barrier west of Jerusalem violated the rights of Palestinians and ordered 30 km of existing and planned barrier to be rerouted; but ruled the barrier is legal in essence and accepted the government's security justification[citation:11]

legal.name: Advisory Opinion on the Legal Consequences of the Construction of a Wall in the Occupied Palestinian Territory (2004) — International Court of Justice (ICJ)
legal.desc: Found that the construction of the wall, and its associated regime, are contrary to international law; cannot rely on a right of self-defense or state of necessity to preclude wrongfulness[citation:11]

legal.name: Death Penalty for Terrorism Law (2026) — Knesset (Israeli Parliament)
legal.desc: Passed by 62-48 vote making death penalty the default punishment for Palestinians convicted in military courts of killing Israelis; applies to Palestinians under Military Order 1651 but not to Israeli settlers tried in civilian courts[citation:13]

legal.name: Criminal law / Death penalty
legal.desc: System of capital punishment applied to one national group (Palestinians) but not another (Israeli settlers) within the same territory. Palestinians are subject to military courts with 96% conviction rate and mandatory death penalty; Israelis are tried in civilian courts. Procedural differences include: unanimity required for civilian death sentences reduced to majority for military courts, elimination of military commander's power to commute sentences, prohibition of pardons, 90-day execution mandate, and restricted appeals. 93% of complaints regarding settler violence against Palestinians are closed without charges filed.[citation:13]

legal.name: Land ownership / Property law
legal.desc: Israel's security cabinet repealed Law No. 40, opening Israeli land purchases in the West Bank. Previously, this law restricted land sales to Arab buyers to prevent Israeli settlement. The change allows settlement expansion that could undermine Palestinian sovereignty and statehood. Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich stated: 'We will continue to kill the idea of a Palestinian state.'[citation:10]

legal.name: Planning and Construction law
legal.desc: Israel uses Military Order 418 to control all planning and construction in Area C. The Civil Administration bans Palestinian construction while encouraging settlement development through a parallel mechanism. A parallel planning mechanism grants approvals for settlers while ignoring their building violations.[citation:1]

legal.name: الآثار القانونية المترتبة على سياسات إسرائيل وممارساتها في الأرض الفلسطينية المحتلة (2024) — محكمة العدل الدولية
legal.desc: أعلنت المحكمة أن احتلال إسرائيل للأراضي الفلسطينية غير قانوني، ويجب إنهاؤه 'في أقرب وقت ممكن'. قرارات الضم والاستيطان وتهجير السكان 'باطلة تماماً ولا يمكن أن تغير الوضع القانوني للأراضي المحتلة' [citation:1][citation:8].

legal.name: الآثار القانونية لبناء جدار في الأرض الفلسطينية المحتلة (2004) — محكمة العدل الدولية
legal.desc: بناء الجدار ونظامه المرافق يتعارض مع القانون الدولي؛ لا يمكن الاعتماد على حق الدفاع عن النفس أو ضرورة الحالة لتبرير المخالفة [citation:1].

legal.desc: حددت الجمعية العامة أن دولة فلسطين مؤهلة للعضوية الكاملة في الأمم المتحدة [citation:1].

legal.name: قانون الأراضي والملكية
legal.desc: في فبراير 2026، وافق مجلس الأمن الإسرائيلي على سلسلة من القرارات تسمح للإسرائيليين بشراء الأراضي في الضفة الغربية، وإلغاء القوانين الأردنية التي تحكم ملكية الأراضي منذ 1967. يصف الخبراء هذا بأنه انتهاك لقرارات مجلس الأمن 242 و446 و2334 وقد يرقى إلى جريمة حرب. استئناف عملية تسجيل الأراضي سيؤدي إلى تهجير منهجي للفلسطينيين حيث أن 70% من أراضي الضفة غير مسجلة وغير مثبتة الملكية [citation:4][citation:8].

legal.name: قانون التخطيط والبناء
legal.desc: تستخدم إسرائيل الأمر العسكري رقم 418 للسيطرة على جميع عمليات التخطيط والبناء في المنطقة (ج). تمنع الإدارة المدنية الإسرائيلية البناء الفلسطيني بينما تشجع تطوير المستوطنات من خلال آلية موازية تمنح الموافقات للمستوطنين وتتجاهل انتهاكات البناء الخاصة بهم. يفرض هذا النظام تمييزاً واضحاً في الحق في السكن والتنمية [citation:1].
legal.perspective: السلطة الوطنية الفلسطينية / دائرة الأراضي / سلطة المياه / الجهاز المركزي للإحصاء

legal.name: القانون الجنائي / عقوبة الإعدام
legal.desc: نظام عقوبة الإعدام يطبق على الفلسطينيين في المحاكم العسكرية (معدل إدانة 96%) ولكن لا يطبق على المستوطنين الإسرائيليين في المحاكم المدنية. الاختلافات الإجرائية تشمل: إلغاء اشتراط الإجماع في أحكام الإعدام، منع العفو، مهلة تنفيذ 90 يوماً، تقييد الطعون. 93% من شكاوى العنف الاستيطاني ضد الفلسطينيين تغلق دون توجيه تهم [citation:1].

legal.name: Proclamation No. 2 Concerning Regulation of Authority and Law (1967) — Officer Commanding IDF Forces in the Area
legal.desc: Vested full governing, legislative, appointment and administrative authority over the area in the IDF area commander; the military commander is treated as the source of governing authority, bounded by art. 43 of the Hague Regulations (1907) — duty to ensure public order and safety while respecting local law in force before the takeover — with residual (security) legislative authority exercised through military orders. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: Emergency Regulations (Judea and Samaria — Jurisdiction over Offenses and Legal Assistance), 5727-1967, extended through 15 February 2028
legal.desc: Grants Israeli civilian courts extraterritorial criminal and civil jurisdiction over Israelis for acts committed in the area, regulates Israel Police authority to operate there, and provides a statutory basis for service of process, fine collection, enforcement and legal assistance vis-à-vis the Palestinian Authority; renewed periodically by Knesset primary legislation (most recently the 5783-2023 extension law). [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: Order Concerning the Establishment of a Civil Administration (Judea and Samaria) (No. 947), 5742-1981
legal.desc: Established the Civil Administration, subordinate to the Coordinator of Government Activities in the Territories (COGAT) at the Ministry of Defense, responsible for licensing, land, water, environmental quality, building supervision, archaeology, transportation and civil-security coordination. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: Order Concerning Regional Councils (Judea and Samaria) (No. 783), 5739-1979 and Order Concerning Local Councils (Judea and Samaria) (No. 892), 5741-1981
legal.desc: Established municipal governance frameworks incorporating Israeli administrative and municipal legislation into security legislation, applied territorially to Israeli communities in the area, enabling municipal services, local planning, education, health and welfare. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: Order Concerning Government Property (Judea and Samaria) (No. 59), 5727-1967, applied with the Ottoman Land Code (1858)
legal.desc: Statutory basis for declaring unregistered miri/mawat land as government property, following the methodology developed after HCJ 390/79 (Elon Moreh): aerial-photo and field survey by the Custodian of Government Property, public notice with maps, a 45-day statutory objection period, and adjudication by an appeals committee established under Order Concerning Appeals Committees (No. 172), 5728-1967, before a declaration becomes final. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: HCJ 390/79 Elon Moreh (Dweikat v. Government of Israel) (1979) — Israeli Supreme Court
legal.desc: Held that military seizure orders over privately-held land may not be used for the purpose of establishing permanent civilian settlement, prompting reliance instead on state-land declaration procedures under the Ottoman Land Code framework rather than military requisition for such purposes. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: "Blue Line Team" land-status verification methodology (established 1999, Civil Administration); upheld in HCJ 8395/14 and HCJ 13080/17
legal.desc: A Civil Administration unit re-examining 1980s–1990s state-land declaration boundaries using geodetic and GIS survey tools, capable of both reducing declared area where evidence of prior cultivation is found and refining/extending boundaries where mawat/uncultivated miri status is confirmed; its process was upheld as a proper, professional administrative procedure by the Supreme Court. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: Order Concerning Town, Village and Building Planning Law (Judea and Samaria) (No. 418), 5731-1971
legal.desc: Amended Jordanian Planning Law No. 79 of 1966, centralizing national and district planning authority in the Civil Administration's Supreme Planning Council (SPC), which operates subcommittees for settlement planning, planning and licensing, and enforcement; all construction, infrastructure development or land use in Area C is stated to require a building permit issued under an approved detailed outline plan. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: Interim Agreement on the West Bank and the Gaza Strip (Oslo II), signed Washington, 28 September 1995, given effect via Proclamation Concerning Implementation of the Interim Agreement (Judea and Samaria) (No. 7), 5756-1995
legal.desc: Statutory basis for the Areas A/B/C division: Area A (~18%, full PA civil and security responsibility, subject to residual Israeli self-defense/counter-terrorism authority), Area B (~22%, PA civil authority, shared Israeli security responsibility), Area C (~60%, full Israeli civil and security authority) — defined as remaining in force pending a permanent-status agreement, and justified additionally on grounds of civilian safety, freedom of movement on main routes, border defense and strategic interests. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: Interim Agreement Annex III, Protocol Concerning Civil Affairs, Article 40 — Joint Water Committee (JWC)
legal.desc: Statutory basis for water-resource allocation from the Mountain Aquifer's three basins (Western, North-Eastern, Eastern), setting fixed annual pumping quotas per side; the JWC (equal Israeli/Palestinian representation) must unanimously approve new well drilling, water/wastewater infrastructure and quota changes; Israel is stated to be in full compliance with its obligations and, via Mekorot, to supply quantities exceeding the amounts originally set in the Oslo-era documents. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: HCJ 2056/04 Beit Sourik Village Council v. Government of Israel (2004) — Israeli Supreme Court
legal.desc: Recognized the military commander's authority to construct a security barrier on purely security grounds, but subjected route selection to a three-part proportionality test (rational connection, least-restrictive alternative, proportionality stricto sensu); invalidated specific segments causing disproportionate harm to agricultural life and ordered rerouting, leading to a 20 February 2005 government decision on a revised barrier route. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]

legal.name: HCJ 7957/04 Mara'abe v. Prime Minister of Israel (Alfei Menashe enclave) (2005) — Israeli Supreme Court
legal.desc: Held that the military commander's authority under Hague Regulation 43 extends to protecting the lives and safety of all persons present in the held territory, including Israeli civilians resident in settlements, and declined to follow the ICJ's 2004 advisory opinion for want of a developed security factual record before that tribunal. [from the Israeli-perspective source report; the corresponding Palestinian-perspective West Bank source report has not yet been supplied for this dataset]
